# The Office Girl — A Day in the Bdsm Corporate World

---

## Her Appearance

Maya arrives at the Nexus Building each morning looking nothing like any secretary from the world outside. Her "uniform" is standardized across all floor girls — a full-body latex catsuit in corporate charcoal grey, so thin and tight it reads more like a second skin than clothing, every curve and contour mapped perfectly beneath it. The material is semi-transparent at the torso panel, making the flesh beneath glow faintly pink under the fluorescent office lighting.

Her nipples are pierced with small gold rings — company-issued hardware — from which hang laminated ID badges bearing her employee number, department code, and a small QR code that supervisors scan to pull her performance record. No name. Just the number. Her collar is stiff posture-training leather, polished black, fitted with a steel ring at the throat and a thin cable that runs to a small monitoring device clipped at the back — it tracks her heart rate, stress levels, and arousal metrics, all feeding live into the department dashboard.

Her hair is pulled back tightly, regulation bun, with a latex headband. Her mouth is lightly stretched by a small permanent-wear lip ring that makes speaking possible but gives her words a soft, helpless quality her supervisors find — efficient. Heels are mandatory, locked ankle-height platforms in matching latex, with small locks at the buckle. She does not have a key.

Her wrists carry thin steel cuffs, decorative in appearance but functional — they clip to desk restraint points during certain task periods.

---

## Her Workstation

The open-plan floor houses forty girls, each at an identical black desk. The chairs are the first thing any visitor notices — or rather the absence of chairs. Each workstation has a mounting post rising from the floor, adjusted to individual height during onboarding and then locked there permanently. At the top of the post is a smooth, firm silicone shaft, company-branded, in the same charcoal grey as the uniforms.

The morning ritual is observed: Maya pulls the crotch-panel of her catsuit aside via its single small zipper, positions herself over the post, and lowers herself slowly until she is seated — the shaft fully inside her, the base plate flat against her, the zipper re-sealed. There is a thin locking tab. A supervisor walks the rows with a small key tool each morning, seating the locks in place. She is now, technically, fixed to her workstation.

The posts are not static. Each one is connected to the building's automated incentive system. When her productivity metrics drop below threshold — response time on requests, accuracy scores, client satisfaction ratings — the post activates, a slow pulse, until numbers climb again. When she exceeds targets, there is a different setting. The girls learn very quickly to want to exceed targets.

Her desk has no drawers. Storage is not her business. Her computer monitor is mounted at standing height so she must look slightly upward at all times — a posture the company documentation describes as *attentive and receptive*. Her keyboard is standard except the keys are slightly smaller, requiring precision, and any error triggers a small shock from the wrist cuffs. Not damaging. Just present. The girls type very carefully.

---

## Her Tasks and Responsibilities

**Maya is a Processing Girl, Level 2.**

Her primary task is Request Fulfillment — the company operates as a high-end service house, and clients submit requests through a portal. Maya's job is to read each request, categorize it, prepare the fulfillment package, and route it to the appropriate department. The requests themselves are detailed, specific, and often bizarre. She handles them with the blank professional efficiency she has been trained into. She does not have opinions about requests. She was corrected out of that during onboarding.

Secondary tasks include:

**Body Correspondence.** Certain premium clients prefer their messages delivered physically rather than digitally. Maya will be fitted with a small capsule — a document container — inserted internally, sealed, and she will be walked by runner escort to the client's floor or office suite, where the item is retrieved. This is logged as a delivery. It appears on her performance sheet as a green tick.

**Display Availability.** On the hour, every hour, all Processing Girls minimize their screens, sit fully upright, hands flat on the desk, and hold still for sixty seconds while floor supervisors perform a visual audit. Any girl found with poor posture, misaligned uniform, or sub-threshold arousal metrics (the monitoring collar reports) is noted. Three notes in a day mean an afterhours correction session.

**Client Reception.** When a floor client visits in person, the nearest available girl — determined by the desk proximity algorithm — must stand, present herself at the door threshold, and remain in greeting position (hands clasped behind, chin slightly down, weight on both heels) for the duration of the client's time on the floor. She does not speak unless addressed. She is, functionally, a living piece of reception furniture.

**Report Generation.** Once per day, Maya must compile her own performance metrics into a written self-assessment and submit it to her supervisor. The reports are written in third person. She refers to herself as *the unit.* Supervisors have found this format reduces emotional noise in the data.

---

## Lunch

There is no lunch break in the conventional sense.

At midday, the floor girls are unclipped from their posts by supervisors — a slow, deliberate process, each girl lifted and walked on slightly unsteady legs to the Refueling Room. The room has no tables or chairs. Along one wall are row-mounted feeding stations — girls step up to a platform, a nozzle is inserted through the mouth-ring, and a nutritional formula is delivered on a timer. Enough. Efficient. Their hands are clipped behind them during this period. They cannot feed themselves. They are fed.

The room is also used for midday correction if the morning session has produced enough noted infractions. There are six stations along the opposite wall for this purpose. The other girls watch while they feed. This is considered part of the incentive structure.

After precisely twenty-two minutes, they are walked back to the floor, re-seated, locked, and the afternoon session begins.

---

## The Night Storage — The Hanging Wall

At exactly 7 PM, the floor empties.

But not in the way normal workers leave offices.

The Storage Corridor is at the back of the building on each floor — a long, climate-controlled room kept at body temperature, lit in deep red. Along both walls, from floor to near-ceiling, are mounted horizontal brackets in rows, numbered and labeled, each corresponding to a specific girl. This is where Maya sleeps.

The preparation takes forty minutes and is performed by the night-shift processing team.

First: the catsuit is removed and replaced with the sleep unit — a full enclosure latex suit in deep black, heavier material, internally lined with conductive gel. The suit has no openings. Every aperture is sealed before the outer layer is applied. The face is covered completely — only a thin breathing tube protrudes at the nostril position, barely visible. The suit is then vacuum-compressed, drawing tight against the body until there is effectively no space between the latex and the skin beneath. The figure that results is smooth, featureless, the shape of a woman but abstract, like a store mannequin sealed inside black glass.

All holes are filled before sealing. This is part of the sleep protocol — the company documentation describes it as *maintaining continuous occupancy for threshold maintenance.* The items are fixed internally, connected via thin cable to the suit's monitoring system, which continues logging data through the night. Her arousal metrics, her biometrics, her sleep-state indicators — all running, all recorded, all informing the next day's baseline settings for her post.

The sealed form is then placed horizontally onto her bracket — her numbered shelf — and the outer restraint harness is applied. This is a rigid external shell, articulated carbon-fiber, that locks around the latex-sealed body and fixes it to the shelf mount completely. She cannot shift her weight. She cannot turn. She cannot flex her fingers. The harness holds her in the same neutral position — arms flat at sides, legs together, head level — from lock-in to release. This position does not change for the duration.

The girls hang in their rows like inventory. Like garments on a warehouse rack.

From outside the room's small observation window, a person could stand and look down the rows and see forty sealed black forms, perfectly still, breathing in the faintest rhythmic movement of the latex over the chest, uniform in their packaging, indistinguishable from one another without reading the shelf numbers.

The supervisors find this room very efficient.

---

## Why She Works So Hard

This is the thing that makes the system elegant, from a managerial perspective.

The night wall is not comfortable. The wall is endurable. There is no position change, no relief, no stimulation that responds to her — only the fixed, present, immovable fullness of the sealed suit, and the darkness, and the silence, and the nine hours until the harness unclicks.

The workday — the post, the incentive pulses, the exceeded-target rewards, the physical tasks, the midday correction room, all of it — is, by comparison, *relief.* It is sensation that responds. It is movement. It is the ability to affect her own experience through performance.

Maya has been in the system for eight months. She is a consistently high performer. She types very fast and very accurately. She exceeds her fulfillment targets four days out of five. She has not required a correction station visit in six weeks.

She works hard because working is the closest thing to freedom the building offers her.

Her supervisors call this *appropriate motivation alignment.*

---

## The Weekly Selection — The Disappearing Girl

Every Friday at 4 PM, the floor quiets.

The wall screen at the front of the processing floor — normally displaying productivity dashboards and client queues — switches over. It shows only a simple graphic: the storage corridor schematic, all forty shelf positions rendered as small rectangles. And then, one by one, they are greyed out. The selection algorithm runs. It takes about thirty seconds.

One shelf number remains lit.

The other girls look at it. They look at each other. The atmosphere on the floor changes in a way the monitoring systems record but the supervisors pretend not to see in the data — a collective spike, complex, not cleanly categorized as either the fear metric or the arousal metric, often both simultaneously.

The girl whose shelf number is displayed will, tonight, not be placed in her normal storage unit.

She will be taken instead to the Sub-Level.

What happens in the Sub-Level is not communicated to the floor girls. It is never described in the company documentation. The girl does not return to her shelf. Her workstation is found empty on Monday morning — the post still in place, the desk still numbered, the ID badge eventually removed by facilities.

A new girl begins onboarding, usually by Wednesday.

The system does not explain. The floor does not ask. The selection is random, audited by an external algorithm the supervisors themselves do not control, which may or may not be true, and the uncertainty about whether it is true or not is itself a feature of the system rather than a flaw in it.

Maya has watched the screen every Friday for eight months. She has watched six shelf numbers light up. She has watched six desks go quiet.

She does not know if working harder changes the probability. The company has neither confirmed nor denied this. There are girls on the floor who believe it does. There are girls who believe the algorithm is truly blind. There are girls who believe the selection is not random at all but follows a pattern no one has yet correctly identified, and these girls spend part of their processing time — logged as idle deviation, which costs them incentive points — trying to map the six disappeared girls against performance records, seniority, physical characteristics, anything.

None of them have published a conclusion.

Friday at 4 PM remains the longest thirty seconds of Maya's week.

On Friday evenings, after the screen resets, she always exceeds her afternoon targets by a considerable margin.

Her supervisor notes this in her record as *exemplary stress-response productivity.*

It is marked in green.
